text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eyes are on key Islamist MP Aydin Menderes amid rumours that he will resign from his party and deal a body blow to the Islamist-conservative government.
- Two rebel conservative ministers predict the government will fall soon.
- A record number of pistols were sold in Turkey last year.
- Loss-making state companies are beginning to perform better, with 25 out of 49 firms posting profits in 1996.
- Seventy-four people have died in car crashes since the start of a week-long holiday on Thursday afternoon and officials fear that the toll will mount.
- Woods around Istanbul are being stripped of their legal protection and being sold to "property mafias" for development.

- President Suleyman Demirel is planning to call a new summit of party leaders if a meeting on Saturday of top military and government figures fails to resolve problems between the secularist army and the Islamist-conservative coalition.
